title: How I'm Investing With $1.5 Million Stock Portfolio
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; captions readable, minor auto-caption garbling of names
summary: Joseph Carlson walks through his real $1.5M portfolio holding by holding (portfolio up $57k; 2026 YTD -1.28%, trailing the S&P 500). Top position Google (~$200k, +$18k): he holds despite concern that Google has fallen behind in the AI model race (Gemini lagging ChatGPT and Claude), citing a reasonable 25 forward PE, ~23% revenue growth, YouTube worth ~$1T (ads +12%, subscriptions +17%), cloud +57% and a backlog above $500B (+374%); he would strongly consider trimming at 30 PE. Meta: holding, still undervalued at 23 forward PE; discusses Meta hiring MongoDB's active CEO a day before its investor day to lead enterprise AI (Meta Enterprise platform, Muse Agent, Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code) and calls the market's -4% reaction misguided. Mastercard ($190k, +$42k): untouched — >50% margins deserve a high-20s multiple, growing in every region. Amazon (12%, $180k, +$55k): not overvalued at 26 PE, well positioned for agentic commerce. ASML ($126k, +$93k gains): holding as China sales mix fell from ~50% to ~14%, derisking the investment. New/explicit calls: S&P Global is 'a buy today' (21 fwd PE; ETF-linked AUM $3T to $6T; AI data fears short-sighted); Texas Roadhouse 'a buy today' after a 21% selloff on temporary beef-inflation pressure (-16% net income) while all sales metrics grow; Uber 'way undervalued' at $68 (17 fwd PE; robotaxi fears more than priced in). Netflix the 'most undervalued' in his portfolio (PE crushed from 50 to 22; engagement up 2% YoY). Holds Costco and DoorDash ('continuing to hold'). Also: Jensen Huang vs Andrew Yang on AI automation (he argues automation is positive-sum, not zero-sum) and Bob Iger as his 'fail of the week' over the Chapek succession saga.
